1.  Tree City U.S.A. 2024 Award and Recognition of the Arbor Day 2025
  Poster Contest Winners
  The City Council will receive and file the Tree City U.S.A. 2024 Award from the
  National Arbor Day Foundation, and recognition awards will also be presented
  to the winners of the Arbor Day 2025 Poster Contest from Bandini Elementary
  School and Rosewood Park School.

2.  Certificate of Recognition for the Commerce Evening Lions Club on the
  Occasion of Celebrating its 50th Anniversary
  Attachments:  Lions Club

PUBLIC COMMENT
Citizens wishing to address the City Council and Successor Agency on any item on the agenda or on any matter
not on the agenda may do so at this time. State law (Government Code Section 54950 et seq.) prohibits the City
Council from taking action or engaging in discussion on a specific item unless it appears on a posted agenda .
Upon request, the City Council may, in their discretion, allow citizen participation on a specific item on the agenda
at the time the item is considered by the City Council. If you wish to address the City Council /Successor Agency
at this time, please complete a speaker's card and give it to the City Clerk prior to commencement of the City
Council meeting. Please limit your remarks to three (3) minutes.

To increase the effectiveness of the Public Comment Period, the following rules shall be followed: No person shall
make any remarks which result in disrupting, disturbing or otherwise impeding the meeting.

Pursuant to Section 54957.95 of the Government Code, the presiding member of the legislative body conducting a
meeting, or their designee, is authorized to remove, or cause the removal of, an individual for disrupting the
meeting. Any such removal will be preceded by a warning to the disruptive individual by the presiding member of
the legislative body or their designee that the individual ’s behavior is disrupting the meeting and that the individual ’s
failure to promptly cease their disruptive behavior may result in their removal.

minutes_text:
AGENDA ITEMS AND ACTIONS
5:00 P.M. CLOSED SESSION

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Altamirano called the meeting to order at 5:01 p.m.

ROLL CALL

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION ITEMS There were no individuals wishing to address the City Council on any items on Closed Session agenda. 

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION City Council/Successor Agency recessed to Closed Session at 5:02 p.m.

RECONVENE TO OPEN SESSION City Council/Successor Agency reconvened to Open Session at 6:17 p.m.

ORAL CLOSED SESSION ANNOUNCEMENT City Attorney Tapia reported on the Closed Session items, noting that two potential litigation matters were discussed. For one of the items, Councilmember Rebollo was not present and did not participate in the discussion.

Regarding Item #1, City staff delivered a presentation, the City Council provided direction, and no reportable action was taken on either item.

6:00 P.M. - CITY COUNCIL MEETING

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Altamirano called a regular meeting to order at 6:18 p.m.

ROLL CALL

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE Parks and Recreation Director Alaniz led the Pledge of Allegiance

INVOCATION Councilmember Garcia offered the invocation

APPEARANCES AND PRESENTATIONS

2.. Certificate of Recognition for the Commerce Evening Lions Club on the Occasion of Celebrating its 50th Anniversary Mayor Altamirano presented a Certificate of Recognition to the Lions Club, acknowledging their outstanding service and continued contributions to the community. Councilmember Argumedo shared that both he and his wife are proud members of the Lions Club and expressed his gratitude for the opportunity to serve and volunteer alongside such a dedicated organization.

Mayor Altamirano also announced that Certificates of Recognition will be issued to the Bell Gardens High School Girls Varsity Volleyball Team in honor of their remarkable 2024 season. Councilmember Rebollo spoke with pride about the team’s historic achievement, highlighting their hard work and determination in capturing their first-ever CIF title.


1.. Tree City U.S.A. 2024 Award and Recognition of the Arbor Day 2025 Poster Contest Winners The City of Commerce Public Works Department proudly recognized the talented winners of the Arbor Day 2025 Poster Contest during a special presentation. 

Alex Villalta, Forestry Assistant for the Los Angeles County Fire Department, delivered remarks about the significance of Arbor Day and the City’s continued commitment to urban forestry. He also acknowledged the City of Commerce for receiving a prestigious award in recognition of its efforts to maintain and grow its urban trees.

PUBLIC COMMENT Gloria Nezahualcoytl recommended utilizing local artists for future City art projects and suggested a specific artist for consideration. She also commended City Council and staff for their continued dedication to the community and reminded the Council of the importance of recognizing and rewarding employees, including through raises when appropriate.

Lee Squire, Downey resident and a veteran, expressed his gratitude to the City for hosting the Military Appreciation Ceremony. He also spoke about the importance of Memorial Day and the significance of honoring those who made the ultimate sacrifice.




CONSENT CALENDAR  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Kevin Lainez

4.. Memorandum of Understanding with the Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority for Measure R 20% Bus Operation Funds

5.. Contract Extension Agreement with Granicus Legistar Agenda Management Software and Services

3.. Approval of Warrant Register Nos. 20A, 20B, 20C, and 20D

6.. Agreement with Keenan & Associates for Self-Insured Claims Administration

SCHEDULED MATTERS

8.. PRESENTATION/UPDATE FROM THE SHERIFF'S DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC SAFETY IN THE CITY OF COMMERCE

9.. Aquatics Facility Fence Project Director of Parks and Recreation Alaniz provided an overview of the item.

Councilmember Rebollo inquired whether all gates would be able to be opened when needed. Director Alaniz confirmed that all gates will be accessible and that staff will be able to bring necessary equipment through them.

Councilmember Argumedo asked if any bushes would be removed. Director Alaniz explained that at one gate, the existing bushes will remain, while the other three gated areas will receive new shrubbery. The only location without greenery will be the access point designated for equipment entry.

A discussion followed regarding the design and the final appearance of the project. Councilmember Argumedo recommended incorporating a community-focused element into the design. City Manager Hernandez suggested returning with two additional renderings. As a result, the item was continued.

7.. Resolution Designating the City of Commerce as a Purple Heart City & Presenting  Commendation Honoring Purple Heart Recipients Mayor Altamirano thanked Lee Squire and Councilmember Garcia for bringing forward the initiative to designate the City of Commerce as a Purple Heart City. The Mayor then proceeded to read the official proclamation.

Lee Squire expressed his gratitude for the City’s recognition of Purple Heart recipients and proudly presented a POW flag to the Mayor and City Council in honor of this designation.

11.. Consideration of Converting Ad Hoc Committees (Food & Brewery and Arts in Public Places) into Standing Committees City Manager Hernandez provided an overview of the staff report.

Mayor Altamirano expressed his desire to expand Councilmember involvement in key community initiatives and transformational projects. He requested that Councilmember Rebollo join him and Mayor Pro Tem Lainez for participation in the Veil Food and Brewery District efforts.

Councilmember Lainez inquired whether the Standing Committees would remain advisory in nature and continue to present recommendations to the full City Council for approval. Mayor Altamirano clarified that Standing Committees are composed of three Councilmembers. City Attorney Tapia further explained that although these committees are formed with three members and are governed by the Brown Act, they remain advisory bodies. City Attorney Tapia emphasized that implementation decisions must still come before the full Council unless the Council delegates specific decision-making authority to the committees.

Following discussion, Councilmember Argumedo moved, and Councilmember Garcia seconded, the following Standing Committee appointments: 

Rosewood Side Food and Brewery District Standing Committee: Councilmember Argumedo, Mayor Altamirano, and Councilmember Garcia

Veil Food and Brewery District Standing Committee: Mayor Altamirano, Mayor Pro Tem Lainez, and Councilmember Rebollo

Arts in Public Places Standing Committee: Mayor Altamirano, Councilmember Garcia, and Councilmember Argumedo

The motion carried with the following vote:

AYES: Councilmembers Argumedo, Garcia, Rebollo, Mayor Pro Tem Lainez and Mayor Altamirano (5)




10.. Authorization to Release a Request for Proposals (RFP) for a Rail Feasibility Study  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Ivan Altamirano City Manager Hernandez provided an overview of the item. Mayor Altamirano noted that this initiative was brought forward by Councilmember Argumedo.

Councilmember Argumedo emphasized that traffic congestion remains a significant issue in the area and described the proposal as a realistic solution. He stated that the project should be constructed above ground and expressed concern that previously appropriated funds were not followed up on. He recommended moving forward with a Request for Qualifications (RFQ) to assess the project's feasibility. 





CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY REPORTS Councilmember Argumedo reported attending the Contract Cities Conference, which he described as informative, but noted that the ICSC Conference in Las Vegas was especially beneficial for the City. He shared updates on new development projects, including upcoming fast food establishments and a proposed project that would help fulfill the vision for the Telegraph Corridor. He also announced that the Citadel will be adding a new hotel with upscale restaurants and decorative fountains at the entrance.

Councilmember Rebollo reported attending the Contract Cities Conference and shared that she was reinstalled as a member of the Executive Board. She invited the community to attend the City’s birthday celebration on Saturday. Councilmember Rebollo also extended her condolences to the Transportation Department on the passing of Jose Castillo, noting his outstanding service and that he will be greatly missed.

Councilmember Garcia reported that she attended the Contract Cities Conference. Although she was unable to attend the Memorial Day ceremony, she thanked staff for the presentation honoring fallen heroes. She also expressed appreciation to the City Council for supporting her request to designate the City of Commerce as a Purple Heart City.

Mayor Pro Tem Lainez reported attending the Contract Cities Conference and congratulated Councilmember Rebollo on her reappointment to the Executive Board. He also participated in the ICSC Conference and joined the Public Works team for lunch. He attended the Memorial Day Ceremony at Park Lawn Cemetery to honor and remember fallen heroes. Mayor Pro Tem Lainez also extended his condolences to the family of Jose Castillo.

Mayor Altamirano called for a moment of silence in memory of Jose Castillo. He shared that he attended both the Contract Cities and ICSC conferences. He mentioned a presentation exploring the introduction of pickleball in the community. Mayor Altamirano also shared a personal update, noting he recently traveled to Hawaii to visit his son, who is serving in the U.S. Marine Corps.

ADJOURNMENT Meeting adjourned at 8:12 pm in memory of Jose Castillo, City employee.

Written materials distributed to the City Council are available for public inspection immediately following the posting of this agenda (at least 72 hours prior to a regular City Council meetings) in the City Clerk's Office, at Commerce City Hall, 2535 Commerce Way, Commerce, California, and the Central Library, 5655 Jillson Street, Commerce, California.


Meeting facilities are accessible to persons with disabilities. ln compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, notify the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 722-4805 at least 24 hours prior to the meeting.
